Energy

Harbour town backs tidal power plan

The council voted eleven to two on Thursday to let engineers test three small turbines off the north breakwater, the first tidal project on this stretch of coast.

By Mara Ellison, energy correspondent
14 March 2026
Share on X Share on email

Tidal power has long been the quiet cousin of wind on this coast. The tide is predictable to the minute, but the machines that harvest it have been expensive to build and hard to keep working in salt water. Supporters argue that a small trial is the only honest way to find out what the harbour can give.

Engineers say the channel between the breakwater and the old pier carries water at more than two metres a second at the height of the spring tides. That is enough, they estimate, to run three turbines that together would meet the evening demand of about four hundred homes. The full assessment is published on the council website.

Advertisement

Not everyone is convinced. Fishing crews who work out of the harbour worry about the turbines' effect on the channel, and a local sailing club has asked for a clear route to be kept open during races. The council has promised a review after the first full year.

“We are not building a dam. We are putting three propellers in a fast river that happens to be salt water, and we will take them out again if they do harm.”

The scheme's project lead said the turbines would sit on the seabed and leave more than six metres of clear water above them at the lowest tide.

Next steps

  1. Contractors will survey the seabed this spring.
  2. The turbines arrive by barge in late summer.
  3. A public meeting will report the first results next year.

Residents can comment on the plan until the end of April. The council will publish every comment it receives, without names.
